clue.text: Harry Kane in kinky fetish clothing — he's got some hot booty!

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the second piece is dressed inside the first
kinky means twisted, so the letters of fetish are bent into a new order
to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters of Kane are jumbled

explanation.surface: England's football captain caught in fetish gear, a tabloid scandal about his attractive behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is not the striker's first name here but an anagram signal: NEAK (from Kane) sits inside STHIEF (from fetish, 'kinky'). 'Hot booty' is stolen loot, not a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who steals by stealth carries off hot (stolen) goods, the booty of a burglary.

clue.text: Quiet monastery, energy disconnected, needing renovation

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: disconnected means cut off, so the energy symbol is removed from the monastery word

parts.note: an abbey is a monastery
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A silent religious house, its power supply cut off, in need of a refit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn and run-down is in poor condition and so in want of being done up.

clue.text: Nauseating, upsetting item in the City

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the postcode

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters of item are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Some disturbing news story about the City of London, nauseating stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' reads as an adjective with 'item', but it is the anagram signal; 'the City' is London's financial district, known by its postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that makes you vomit, so as an adjective it means causing sickness.

clue.text: Whence came the knives to stab Harold Wilson's advisers?

definitions.text: Whence came the knives to stab
definitions.meaning: the cupboard in a kitchen where the carving knives are kept
the informal inner circle of unofficial advisers around the 1960s Labour prime minister

explanation.surface: A political assassination question: where did the backstabbers get their blades to bring down the prime minister?
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson was a British Labour prime minister whose close unofficial advisers were nicknamed this; the first reading is a literal cupboard of cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a cupboard in a kitchen and a leader's unofficial circle of trusted aides.

clue.text: Celebrated character of Greene King: fruity flavour

parts.note: Harry is a name for a king, as in Henry V's 'God for Harry'
lime is a citrus fruit flavour

explanation.surface: Greene King is a British brewery; the clue reads like a tasting note for one of its fruity beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greene King' looks like the brewery's name, but it splits: Greene belongs to the definition (the novelist Graham Greene) and King starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Lime is the famous racketeer of Graham Greene's The Third Man.

clue.text: Resistance leader in solitary confinement turned up to register

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from bottom to top, reversing the letters
confinement means being shut in, so the resistance letter is enclosed by the solitary word

parts.note: solitary means lone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter supplies the leader

explanation.surface: A captured Resistance chief, held in solitary, came back to sign on.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside LONE to give LORNE, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or put your name on a list, which is what registering means.

clue.text: Heartless Tolkien monster looking pleased with itself

indicators.note: heartless means losing its centre, so the middle letter is taken away

parts.note: Smaug is the dragon in The Hobbit

explanation.surface: A cruel Tolkien dragon looks self-satisfied, which suits a dragon sitting on its hoard of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone complacently self-satisfied, exactly a pleased-with-oneself look.

clue.text: German nobleman introducing rabbi to Mrs Simpson

indicators.note: introducing means bringing one thing in, so the rabbi goes into Mrs Simpson

parts.note: Marge Simpson, Homer's wife in The Simpsons
rav is a Hebrew title for a rabbi

explanation.surface: A German aristocrat introduces a rabbi to Mrs Simpson, which sounds like Wallis Simpson's society circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs Simpson' suggests Wallis Simpson, but it is the cartoon Marge.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a German nobleman, originally the military governor of a border province.

clue.text: Serve up your wildebeest, pig — fast!

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from bottom to top, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A rushed order to a cook: dish up the wildebeest, you pig, and be quick!
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast!' looks like 'hurry up', but it is the verb: abstain from food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from food, deliberately going without eating.

clue.text: I've cut parental involvement in risky investment

indicators.note: involvement suggests things wound up together, so the letters are entangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A parent explains they have stopped meddling in their child's life, which was a risky thing to invest in.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money put into new businesses with a high chance of loss, a speculative stake.

clue.text: Skilful, can-do expats regularly getting wasted

indicators.note: every other letter is thrown away, leaving alternate letters

explanation.surface: Capable, go-getting expatriates routinely getting drunk abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting wasted' looks like drinking, but it says the odd letters are discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adept means having great proficiency at something, the same as being skilful.

clue.text: Bloody heart-breaking discovery in Ytterby?

parts.note: rare meat is bloody, barely cooked

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the letters of heart are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim, bloody, heartbreaking find at some unfamiliar place.
explanation.walkthrough: Ytterby is a Swedish village whose quarry yielded several of these elements (yttrium, ytterbium, terbium, erbium are named after it).
explanation.definitionFit: Rare-earth elements were famously found in the mine at Ytterby in Sweden, so they are a find made there.

clue.text: "Home Country" — answer to crossword clue in Times

indicators.note: in puts the crossword answer inside the times word

parts.note: by is the multiplication word, as in three by four
a light is a solver's term for an answer in a crossword grid

explanation.surface: A newspaper item: the solution to a Times crossword clue is a phrase meaning home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign. BLIGHTY is old British slang for Britain as home.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighty is affectionate British soldiers' slang for Britain, the homeland.

clue.text: Özil ate Ronaldo's sandwiches afterwards

indicators.note: the outer words enclose the answer the way bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: Footballer Mesut Özil ate Cristiano Ronaldo's sandwiches at some later point.
explanation.definitionFit: Later on is a common phrase for at a subsequent time, meaning afterwards.

clue.text: Plan for doctor with intravenous drip to visit one going loco?

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so the doctor and drip go inside the plan word

parts.note: to engineer something is to plan it
IV is the abbreviation for an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A hospital scheme: a doctor with a drip goes to see a patient who is losing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like 'crazy' but is short for locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: A train driver operates a locomotive, so is the person who drives a loco.

clue.text: Vespers, cantos not covered in common language

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Evening church services and verse cantos are not written in the everyday shared tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto was invented as an international auxiliary language to be shared by everyone.

clue.text: Shellfish overdose; Castro's thrown up

indicators.note: thrown up means tossed about, so the letters of Castro are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Fidel Castro has eaten bad shellfish, overdosed, and vomited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' looks like a reversal in a down clue, but CASTRO is anagrammed to OSTRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostracod is a tiny crustacean with a hinged two-part shell, a seed shrimp.

clue.text: Sussex town band suspended

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, beside Brighton
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: A musical group from a Sussex town has been banned from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a town on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hovering things hang in the air, suspended above the ground.

clue.text: Tempers speed after second time over external drive?

indicators.note: after places the tempers and speed pieces behind the short abbreviations

parts.note: o is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
rages are tempers
pace is speed

explanation.surface: A driver's tantrums at speed, time after time, running over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' looks like motoring, but it is a computer hard drive.
explanation.definitionFit: An external drive is a plug-in device that provides extra room for keeping computer files.

clue.text: Tossed salad infused with liberal quantity of oil produced here

indicators.note: infused with means having something steeped into it, so the liberal letter goes inside
a tossed salad is mixed about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tossed salad dressed with a generous amount of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quantity of' reads as part of the liberal dressing; it links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texas city is at the heart of the American oil industry, as the TV drama about oil barons showed.

clue.text: Good, fine material capturing new look

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the new letter goes into the fabric

parts.note: lace is a fine fabric

explanation.surface: Good quality fine fabric in a fresh style.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look.

clue.text: Hock his 'n' her Rolls

indicators.note: rolls means tumbles over, so these letters are rolled into a new order

explanation.surface: Pawning a couple's matching Rolls-Royce cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' looks like pawning, but it is the German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a British name for German white wine from the Rhine region.

clue.text: Hot, small island, Hispaniola's second republic

parts.note: an ait is a small river island

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hot little island; the second republic on Hispaniola.
explanation.walkthrough: An ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is an independent country sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Jacob's wife turned on hip hop artist

indicators.note: on places the reversed name after the music piece

parts.note: rap is a form of hip hop

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the wife's name is read backwards

parts.note: Leah was Jacob's first wife in Genesis

explanation.surface: The biblical Leah unexpectedly takes up hip hop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacob's wife' tempts RACHEL, but it is her sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was the Italian Renaissance painter of the School of Athens.

clue.text: Key interior design standard

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: design means a planned rearrangement, so the letters of interior are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A key benchmark in interior decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior design' looks like one phrase, but 'design' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard by which something is judged.

clue.text: Time to replace head of hairdressing business, in part to make savage cuts

indicators.note: the first letter of the business word is swapped out for the time letter

parts.note: a salon is a hairdresser's premises

explanation.surface: It is time a hairdressing chain's boss was replaced, partly to make brutal cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' suggests haircuts or job cuts, but the definition is a claw that slashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a bird of prey's claw, the body part it rips prey with.

clue.text: Pursue English magistrate to Venice

parts.note: to dog is to follow persistently

explanation.surface: Chase an English judge all the way to Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of the Venetian republic.

clue.text: Asian State lotteries going bust, swallowing millions

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the millions letter is enclosed
going bust means breaking apart, so the letters of lotteries are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Asian country's state lotteries collapse after eating up millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Timor-Leste, also called East Timor, is an independent nation in Southeast Asia.
